t: You're on Campden Hill, a hill in Kensington, bounded by Holland Park Avenue to the north and Kensington High Street to the south. The name comes from Campden House, built by Baptist Hicks, Viscount Campden, whose country seat was in Chipping Campden in Gloucestershire. Some interesting people lived and died around here. Montagu Norman, Governor of the Bank of England from 1920 to 1944, died here, and so did the writer Violet Hunt, who wrote feminist novels and helped found International PEN. The archaeologist Winifred Lamb was born here.
